image_description: A close-up, slightly low-angle shot of a vintage handheld computer (PDA), likely a Palm Pilot or similar device from the late 90s/early 2000s. The device has a dark grey plastic casing with rounded corners. The screen is monochrome LCD, displaying a handwritten note application with sketches of buildings and text. Below the screen are four physical circular buttons (two on sides, two integrated into a central pill-shaped navigation area). The background is a blurry bright green surface.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The handwritten text on the screen ('Paris', 'Eiffel Tower' labels) is stylistically consistent but slightly illegible and morphs in a way typical of AI-generated text. It mimics handwriting well but lacks perfect character definition upon close inspection.

The plastic buttons have a slightly 'waxy' or overly smooth appearance lacking fine micro-texture or wear marks expected on a used vintage device. The transition between the button and the casing is slightly soft.

artifact_observations.location: Bottom right corner of the device
artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight warping in the curvature of the bottom-right edge of the casing, where the perspective lines do not converge perfectly naturally, suggesting minor geometric instability.

selected_experts.reason: To verify if the specific model details (button layout, screen aspect ratio) align with known real-world PDA classes (e.g., Palm Pilot, Psion) rather than a generic hallucination.
To rigorously analyze the legibility and structural integrity of the handwritten text on the LCD screen, checking for AI-specific text artifacts like melting characters or nonsensical glyphs.

To ensure the physical buttons are topologically distinct from the casing and that the screen boundary is sharp and correctly inset, checking for fusion artifacts common in AI generations of complex interfaces.
To assess the realism of the lighting reflections on the plastic casing and the depth-of-field blur, ensuring they match optical physics rather than generative smoothing.

focus_areas: Legibility and structure of handwritten text on the LCD screen
Topological separation between physical buttons and the main casing
Consistency of plastic material texture and lighting reflections
Geometric correctness of the device's rectangular form factor
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'handwritten' text on the screen. AI often fails to render coherent handwriting, resulting in glyph-like scribbles. Verify if the text is semantically plausible (e.g., recognizable words like 'Paris') or just aesthetic noise. Also, check the button geometry: real PDAs have precise mechanical tolerances; AI often merges buttons into the case or makes them asymmetrical without cause.
